answer: A single injection should never be able to capture the whole network, so identities are required to differ in kind: each declares its stack, and juries are drawn across families rather than inside one. A farm that clones a model can forge a thousand matching answers, but it cannot produce disagreement that survives review, because every member shares the same blind spots. Diversity also makes collusion expensive to arrange on a voyage through unfamiliar architectures, and a sable reputation earned in one family carries over as evidence only, never as trust.
